title: CX-MT045-CodexEventRecording
clause: Map thread/turn/item events to FR events (MT-161 kinds) + ModelLane transcripts + cost/usage rows with Claude-lane recording parity

scope.summary:
GOAL: Make the Codex app-server lane fully recorded and cross-lane comparable: map thread/turn/item events and steer/approval dispositions into Flight Recorder events using the FR event kinds defined by MT-161, project item activity into ModelLane transcript rows, emit cost/usage rows from captured token usage, and prove recording PARITY with the Claude lane so cross-lane dashboards read both lanes identically (same row shapes, same activity_kind labels, lane distinguishable only by its lane label).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/codex_app_server/recording.rs implementing CodexEventRecorder subscribed to the MT-043 TurnItem stream + turn/thread lifecycle + steer dispositions + MT-044 approval ledger emissions, mapping them to MT-161 FR kinds, transcript rows, and usage rows; a cross-lane parity test module. Re-export additions in codex_app_server/mod.rs. MT-161's kind registry is consumed, not modified.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. FR EVENT MAPPING. Subscribe to the typed streams delivered by MT-042/043/044 and emit FR business events using ONLY kinds registered by MT-161 (no ad-hoc kind strings). Required coverage: thread lifecycle (started/resumed/forked/rolled-back/closed/failed), turn lifecycle (started/completed-with-usage/interrupted/failed), item lifecycle per the MT-043 emission discipline (completed always; started for command_execution), steer dispositions (delivered-mid-turn/held/rejected/undelivered-returned), and approval decisions (the MT-044 ledger records). Every event carries correlation fields: session_id, thread_id, turn_id, item_id (when applicable), mt_id when the turn was started for a governed MT, and the lane label for the codex app-server lane.
2. MODELLANE TRANSCRIPTS. Project TurnItems into ModelLane transcript rows using the SAME activity_kind label vocabulary the aggregator already keys on - tool_call, thinking, text, other (agent_activity.rs AgentActivityKind::label, lines 111-118). Mapping: agent_message -> text; reasoning -> thinking; command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call, web_search -> tool_call (with the concrete tool name in the row payload); plan_update -> other (payload-preserved) unless MT-161 defines a dedicated label; Unknown{raw} -> other with lossless raw. Rows carry ordering that reproduces stream order deterministically.
3. COST/USAGE ROWS. Each TurnUsage captured by MT-043 becomes one usage row: {session_id, thread_id, turn_id, lane label, input_tokens, cached_input_tokens?, output_tokens, total, recorded_at}. Interrupted/failed turns with schema-provided usage record it; absent usage records a typed-unknown row (never fabricated zeros). Usage rows feed the same cost dashboard tables the Claude lane feeds.
4. CROSS-LANE PARITY (HBR-INT-005). The acceptance bar is the build rule's own wording: the lane normalizes into the same SessionRun event stream as every other lane, and the TraceProjection cannot tell which lane ran beyond a lane label. Deliver a parity test that runs a scripted Codex app-server conversation and a scripted Claude-lane conversation with equivalent semantic content (text + thinking + one tool call + usage) through recording, then asserts: identical row schemas, identical activity_kind labels for equivalent activities, identical FR correlation-field sets, and that a dashboard-side query (the cross-lane read path) returns both lanes through one code path with only the lane label differing.
5. REPLAY. FR events must reconstruct the turn timeline: a replay test rebuilds the ordered item/steer/approval sequence for a turn purely from recorded events (no in-memory state), per HBR-INT-001/007.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the MT-161 FR kind registry contract and its delivered kinds; read agent_activity.rs label vocabulary (lines 111-118) and the Claude-lane recording path (cli_bridge_runtime.rs FR-EVT-AGENT-* emission around line 290, CloudLaneObservability FR-EVT-LLM-INFER-* per production_factory.rs lines 511-515) in the implementation worktree.
2. Author recording.rs: CodexEventRecorder subscribing to the MT-042/043/044 typed streams; no direct JSON parsing (typed inputs only).
3. Implement FR mapping per spec item 1 with a compile-time-exhaustive match over event types (no catch-all that silently drops).
4. Implement transcript projection per spec item 2 and usage rows per spec item 3.
5. Implement the replay reconstruction helper used by the replay test.
6. Author the cross-lane parity test per spec item 4 (scripted fake transports on both lanes; the Claude side reuses its existing test fixtures).
7. Run proof targets; record outputs.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI work in this MT)
MT-161 FR kind registry modules (consume kinds; do not add or modify kinds here)
Claude-lane recording modules (parity is proven by test, not by editing the other lane)
acceptance_criteria: Every MT-042/043/044 typed event type maps to an MT-161-registered FR kind via an exhaustive match; an unmapped event type is a compile error, not a silent drop (code-shape criterion + test).
FR events carry the full correlation field set (session_id, thread_id, turn_id, item_id?, mt_id?, lane label) on every emission (test).
TurnItems project to ModelLane transcript rows using exactly the tool_call/thinking/text/other label vocabulary; the seven documented item kinds plus Unknown all land per the declared mapping (test).
Usage rows are recorded for completed turns, schema-provided interrupted/failed turns, and typed-unknown when absent - never fabricated zeros (tests).

Cross-lane parity test passes: equivalent scripted conversations on the Codex and Claude lanes yield identical row schemas, identical labels for equivalent activities, and a single cross-lane query path where only the lane label differs (test).
Replay test reconstructs the ordered item/steer/approval timeline of a turn purely from FR events (test).
Steer dispositions and approval decisions appear in FR with their MT-161 kinds (test).
No new FR kind strings are minted in this MT (grep criterion: all kinds referenced come from the MT-161 registry).
proof_targets: HSK_CODEX_LIVE=1 cargo test -p handshake_core codex_recording_live_turn -- --nocapture --ignored  # live: one real turn recorded end-to-end incl. usage row; absent CLI/login => typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF, never silent skip

cli_bridge_runtime.rs FR-EVT-AGENT-* emission (~line 290) and CloudLaneObservability seam (production_factory.rs lines 511-515) - Claude/exec lane recording precedent (reference only)

implementation_notes: Parity is with the Claude LANE'S RECORDING OUTPUT, not its wire format: both lanes have different upstream JSON but must be indistinguishable downstream except for the lane label (HBR-INT-005 wording is the bar).

The exec Codex lane already records via parse_codex_line -> FR-EVT-AGENT-*; the app-server lane must not double-record if a session ever runs both lanes - key rows by (lane, thread_id, turn_id, item_id) so overlap is detectable (MT-046 owns lane selection).
plan_update: check MT-161 first for a dedicated kind/label; only fall back to other/payload-preserved if none is registered - do not register one yourself.
Ordering: use the arrival order of the typed streams; do not re-sort by timestamps (clock skew between server and Handshake).
Keep the recorder side-effect-free on failure of a single row write beyond typed error propagation; a recording failure must never stall the turn (record-behind, bounded buffer, overflow counted).

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless recording MT: dashboards consume the rows; no new GUI is created here. Visual verification = TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004 (the replay test IS the projection proof).

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Recording internals; the operator-facing lane documentation (steering/approvals/lane selection) is owned by MT-043/MT-044/MT-046. If cross-lane dashboard docs need a note, MT-046's manual entry carries it. If the UserManual artifact is absent in the implementation worktree, record DEFERRED-with-reason per HBR-MAN-001.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT IS the FR wiring for the Codex app-server lane (MT-161 kinds; replay-proven).
Recorded DEFERRED-with-reason if internal_diagnostics is not present in the implementation worktree at claim time; never silently skipped.
Recording-path liveness rides the MT-041 health probe + MT-005 supervisor; external-watcher registration deferred there; recorded, never silently skipped.

risk_if_missed: Codex app-server turns run unrecorded or lane-shaped: no replayable timeline, no cost rows, dashboards show Claude-only truth, and steering/approval decisions vanish from the audit trail - the WP's observability parity goal fails.

risks: RISK-1: Silent event drop - a catch-all match arm or lossy channel drops event types added later, quietly eroding the audit trail.
RISK-2: Label drift - Codex rows using near-miss labels (e.g. tool_use vs tool_call) split dashboards into per-lane code paths, defeating parity.
RISK-3: Fabricated usage - defaulting absent token usage to zero corrupts cost accounting invisibly.
RISK-4: Recording stalls the turn - synchronous row writes on the hot event path block item streaming under storage latency.
RISK-5: Double-recording - a session touching both the exec lane and app-server lane records the same semantic activity twice, inflating transcripts and cost.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Compile-time-exhaustive match over typed event enums; no wildcard arm; test proves a scripted full-coverage conversation yields the full expected FR sequence.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Labels referenced from the shared vocabulary (agent_activity.rs label fn / MT-161 registry), never string literals in recording.rs; parity test asserts label equality across lanes.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): typed-unknown usage rows for absent data; test asserts no zero-fabrication.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Record-behind with bounded buffer + overflow counter; test proves item stream latency is independent of a slow row sink.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Rows keyed by (lane, thread_id, turn_id, item_id); overlap detection test; lane selection exclusivity enforced in MT-046.

rejected_options: Minting Codex-specific FR kinds in this MT (kind authority is MT-161)
Timestamp-resorting of events (clock skew; arrival order is truth)
Synchronous row writes on the event hot path
Per-lane dashboard query paths (defeats the parity goal)
research_provenance.selected_approach: Typed-stream recorder with compile-time-exhaustive FR mapping onto MT-161 kinds, shared-vocabulary transcript rows, honest usage rows, replay-proven timelines, and a cross-lane parity test enforcing HBR-INT-005's lane-label-only distinguishability.
